_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for intervals.

questions.title: Overlap rule
questions.prompt: For half-open intervals [start, end), when do [1, 4) and [4, 6) overlap?
choices: They do not overlap because one ends where the other starts
questions.explanation: In a half-open convention, the end value is not included, so touching at 4 is not overlap.

questions.title: Sort first
questions.prompt: Why sort intervals by start before merging?
choices: Nearby overlaps become neighbors in the scan
It changes every end time to zero
questions.explanation: Sorting by start lets one left-to-right pass compare each interval with the current merged range.

questions.title: Merge update
questions.prompt: Merging [1, 5] with [3, 7] should produce what range?
questions.explanation: The merged range keeps the earlier start and the later end.

questions.title: Gap check
questions.prompt: How can a scan tell the next interval starts after the current merged interval?
questions.explanation: If the next start is beyond the current end, there is a gap and a new merged interval begins.

questions.title: Touching policy
questions.prompt: Why must a prompt define whether touching intervals merge?
choices: Because closed and half-open ranges treat endpoints differently
questions.explanation: The condition changes when endpoints touch, so the prompt convention controls the merge rule.

questions.title: Insert interval
questions.prompt: When inserting a new interval into sorted non-overlapping intervals, what should happen first?
choices: Copy intervals that end before the new one starts
Drop intervals after the new one
questions.explanation: Intervals completely before the new range cannot overlap it, so they can be kept first.

questions.title: Covered range
questions.prompt: If [2, 8] already covers [3, 5], what is the merged result?
questions.explanation: The larger range already contains the smaller one, so the outer endpoints stay.

questions.title: Interval mistake
questions.prompt: What is a common interval bug?
choices: Changing the start when only the end should expand
Comparing the next start to the current end
questions.explanation: Most range errors come from including one endpoint too many or too few. Check the interval convention and the update line before changing the whole scan.
